name: What should you do with the pool equipment after removal?

mainEntity.name: What happens to the pump, filter, heater, and other pool equipment after an in-ground pool is removed?
mainEntity.text: What happens to the pump, filter, heater, and other pool equipment after an in-ground pool is removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The pump, filter, heater, automation panel, and other visible equipment are usually disconnected as part of the project. In many cases, the equipment is removed and disposed of, but if components are still in good condition, a homeowner may choose to keep, sell, or repurpose them. The important part is confirming what is included in the contractor’s scope. Some bids cover only shell demolition and backfill, while others include equipment removal, utility disconnects, and cleanup of pads and wiring. In older homes, the equipment may also reveal hidden plumbing or electrical issues that need attention before the yard can be restored. Homeowners should decide early whether they want the equipment removed completely or preserved for resale or future use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool equipment can be removed, recycled, sold, or discarded depending on its condition and the contractor’s scope. If the system is still usable, some homeowners keep or repurpose equipment, but most removal projects include disconnection and disposal. Ask in advance whether equipment removal is included in the bid.
